salient_findings: lytic lesions in the sternum, right humerus, and thoracic vertebrae
key_facts: bilateral pleural and pericardial effusions on chest radiograph and noncontrast chest CT

shortlist.label: Serous carcinoma of the ovary
shortlist.why_kept: elevated CA-125 and PET-CT findings suspicious for primary ovarian malignancy

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral pleural and pericardial effusions, lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: systemic symptoms, lymphadenopathy, and pleural effusions

raw.rationale: Elevated CA-125 level and PET-CT findings suspicious for primary ovarian malignancy, despite normal-sized ovaries on ultrasound, which can occur in early stages of ovarian cancer

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma could explain lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, but the specific findings of elevated CA-125 and PET-CT suspicious for ovarian malignancy are more suggestive of ovarian cancer

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Multiple myeloma could explain lytic bone lesions, but it does not typically cause elevated CA-125 or the specific pattern of pleural and pericardial effusions seen in this case

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, but it does not typically cause elevated CA-125 or the specific pattern of bone lesions and effusions seen in this case

rejected.label: Tuberculosis
rejected.why: Tuberculosis can cause lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, but it does not typically cause elevated CA-125 or the specific pattern of bone lesions and effusions seen in this case, and the patient had a negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR test and no relevant medical history
